Warning: The referenced jira issue has an invalid target version for the target branch this PR targets: expected the sub-task to target the "4.22.0" version, but no target version was set.

<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/cluster-monitoring-operator/pull/2882):

>## Summary
>
>- Bump `library-go`, `api`, and `client-go` to bring in configurable PKI support (library-go PRs #2127, #2145)
>- When the `ConfigurablePKI` feature gate is enabled, resolve key algorithms from the cluster PKI profile for the self-signed GRPC TLS certificates used for Thanos GRPC communication
>- When the feature gate is disabled (default), existing RSA-2048 behavior is preserved
>
>## Details
>
>Certificate names registered with the PKI profile:
>- `monitoring.grpc-tls-signer` — self-signed CA
>- `monitoring.grpc-tls-client` — Thanos querier client cert
>- `monitoring.grpc-tls-serving` — Prometheus GRPC server cert
>
>The implementation switches from the legacy `MakeSelfSignedCAConfig`/`MakeServerCert`/`MakeClientCertificateForDuration` APIs to the new parameterized `NewSigningCertificate`/`NewServerCertificate`/`NewClientCertificate` APIs which properly handle SubjectKeyID computation and KeyUsage flags for all key types.
>
>CSR-based certificates (metrics-client-certs, federate-client-certs, metrics-server-client-certs) are not affected — their keys are already ECDSA and signing is handled by the kube-apiserver.
>
>## Test plan
>
>- [ ] Unit tests pass (`make test-unit`)
>- [ ] CI passes
>- [ ] With `ConfigurablePKI` disabled (default): GRPC TLS certs continue to use RSA-2048
>- [ ] With `ConfigurablePKI` enabled and PKI resource configured: GRPC TLS certs use the configured algorithm

<details>
<summary>📝 Walkthrough</summary>

## Walkthrough

Updated Go module pseudo-versions for OpenShift dependencies in go.mod. RotateGRPCSecret gained a `pki.PKIProfileProvider` parameter and now resolves per-certificate key generators via a new `resolveKeyGenerator` helper, switching to PKI-aware certificate constructors (`crypto.NewSigningCertificate`, `NewClientCertificate`, `NewServerCertificate`) and returning wrapped errors on resolution failures with a fallback to an RSA-2048 generator. Operator was extended to conditionally start a PKI informer when `FeatureGateConfigurablePKI` is enabled and to initialize/store a `pkiProfileProvider`. That provider is injected into `ClusterMonitoringOperatorTask` and propagated to `manifests.RotateGRPCSecret`. Tests were updated to pass `nil` for the new parameter and a new test (`TestRotateGRPCSecretKeyAlgorithm`) was added to verify resolved private-key algorithms via a `keyAlgorithm` helper.

## Estimated code review effort

🎯 3 (Moderate) | ⏱️ ~25 minutes

## Summary

- go.mod: bumped pseudo-versions for OpenShift modules (`github.com/openshift/api`, `github.com/openshift/client-go`, `github.com/openshift/library-go`).
- pkg/manifests/tls.go: changed `RotateGRPCSecret` signature to `RotateGRPCSecret(s *v1.Secret, pkiProvider pki.PKIProfileProvider) error`; added `resolveKeyGenerator` helper; replaced legacy RSA-only certificate/key creation with PKI-aware constructors (`crypto.NewSigningCertificate`, `newCA.NewClientCertificate`, `newCA.NewServerCertificate`); added contextual error wrapping on key-config resolution failures; fallback to legacy `crypto.RSAKeyPairGenerator{Bits: 2048}` when needed.
- pkg/manifests/tls_test.go: updated `RotateGRPCSecret` call sites to include the new parameter (passed as `nil` in existing tests); added `TestRotateGRPCSecretKeyAlgorithm` to assert CA and leaf private-key algorithms for different `pki.PKIProfileProvider` inputs; introduced `keyAlgorithm` helper and extended imports for key parsing and PKI profile configuration.
- pkg/operator/operator.go: added `pkiProfileProvider` field to `Operator`; when `FeatureGateConfigurablePKI` is enabled, registers and starts PKI informer and initializes `o.pkiProfileProvider` via `pki.NewClusterPKIProfileProvider`.
- pkg/tasks/clustermonitoringoperator.go: added `pkiProfileProvider pki.PKIProfileProvider` field to `ClusterMonitoringOperatorTask`; updated constructor signature to accept the provider and changed `Run` to call `manifests.RotateGRPCSecret(s, t.pkiProfileProvider)`.

Review focus: verify key-generator resolution logic and fallback behavior, correctness of error wrapping/context, conditional informer initialization tied to the feature gate, and consistent propagation of the PKI provider through constructors and call sites.

</details>

> LGTM but doesn't the operator need to react and trigger a reconciliation when the pki configuration changes?

No. The new config just gets picked up at the next rotation cycle. This is intentional.

> Do we even need to an informer then? At the very least I'd expect a comment in operator.go explaining that it doesn't need to reconcile the TLS materials ASAP.

Yes, we need the informer so that the PKIProfileProvider can read the PKI resource from the lister cache instead of hitting the API server on every reconciliation. I've added a comment explaining why no event handler is registered: PKI profile changes are picked up at the next certificate rotation cycle, not via immediate reconciliation. 
I also switched from starting the informer manually to adding it to o.informers so its cache is synced before the first reconciliation runs.

/approve

The tech preview job fails because the CMO service accounat has no permissions to list/watch the PKI configuration.
RBAC should be added to `jsonnet/components/cluster-monitoring-operator.libsonnet` then run `make generate` and commit the changes.
